name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground that meets federal motor vehicle safety standards as designed, including a motorbike converted to meet them; an electric one is a motorcycle once its motor exceeds the 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) of a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Idaho Code §49-114(11).

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W), above a motor-driven cycle; ITD treats an electric motor the same as a combustion engine
Meets federal motor vehicle safety standards as originally designed; not a motorbike, moped, motor-driven cycle or electric-assisted bicycle
An off-road motorbike becomes a motorcycle when its owner fits it to meet federal motor vehicle safety standards and Idaho's equipment rules, and self-certifies the conversion on ITD form 3018
Titled, and registered and plated for highway use, or instead issued a restricted vehicle plate or an OHV sticker for OHV roads and trails only
Riders need a valid driver's license with a motorcycle "M" endorsement
An applicant under 21 must complete an approved motorcycle rider training course to get the endorsement
A motorcycle instruction permit allows daylight riding only, with no freeways and no passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a protective helmet, except on private property
With highway plates, may be ridden on all highways, including interstates
